newsitem.title: USA: House committee gets new chief counsel for probe.
newsitem.headline: House committee gets new chief counsel for probe.

text.p: The House committee investigating campaign fund raising scandals in the 1996 election on Tuesday appointed former Maryland federal prosecutor Richard Bennett as chief counsel.
Bennett's appointment to the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee was seen as a signal that the investigation could move into higher gear.
The committee is investigating possible illegal fund raising in the 1996 election campaign, with particular emphasis on the role of foreign money.
It has yet to hold public hearings. Its chairman, Indiana Rep. Dan Burton, is anxious to begin but may have to wait until next year to avoid clashing with Senate hearings.

The Senate Governmental Affairs Committee has held four weeks of hearings which are due to resume in early September. Senate sources said it would make little sense to have simultaneous hearings proceeding in both the House and Senate.
Bennett, an unsuccessful Republican candidate for attorney general of Maryland in 1994, replaces John Rowley who quit the committee citing personal conflicts with its chief investigator.
